content.text:
Fixed.

## Cause

`lib/interceptor/cache.js:322` read the request's cache-control directly off the raw options:

```js
const reqCacheControl = opts.headers?.['cache-control'] ? ... : undefined
```

HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so `{ 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' }` (or any other casing, or a header array/iterable) yielded `undefined` and every client-side directive — `no-store`, `no-cache`, `only-if-cached`, `max-age`, `max-stale`, `min-fresh`, `stale-if-error` — was silently ignored.

## Change

- `lib/interceptor/cache.js`: normalise the request headers once via the existing `normaliseHeaders(opts)` helper (which lowercases keys and also handles iterable header forms), and look up `cache-control` on that. The normalised map is reused for `makeCacheKey` and for the revalidation request headers (`cacheKey.headers`), so this adds no extra normalisation passes — the previous code normalised twice on the revalidation path.
- `lib/util/cache.js`: `makeCacheKey(opts, normalisedHeaders)` now accepts already-normalised headers, falling back to computing them.
- `test/interceptors/cache.js`: added a regression test `no-store w/ a capitalized header name` mirroring the existing `no-store` test, which fails the request if the store is written to.

All 18 tests in `test/interceptors/cache.js` pass. I couldn't run eslint or the temporary revert-to-confirm-failure check — both needed approvals I didn't have — so the new test is verified passing with the fix but not verified red without it; the `'Cache-Control'` → `['cache-control']` lookup returning `undefined` makes that outcome unambiguous, though.
